institution: Istanbul Technical University (İTÜ) — Dr. Erol Üçer Center for Advanced Studies in Music (MIAM)
qualification: Master of Arts (MA) in Music (Müzik Tezli Yüksek Lisans) — thesis master's, second cycle
accreditationStatus: State university, YÖK-accredited; MIAM founded 1999 as Türkiye's first music master's programme
language: ENGLISH-TAUGHT — 100% English. MIAM describes itself as 'Turkey's first music master's program (1999) and music doctoral program (2002) that gives education in %100 English language.'
durationEcts: 2 years (4 semesters), thesis master's; ECTS UNVERIFIED (ITU standard graduate thesis master = 120 ECTS)
whatYouStudy: Electroacoustic/acousmatic composition, sound installation, sound design, live electronic performance, creative audio coding/programming, sonic arts research; MIAM houses a dedicated Sonic Arts Lab. Thesis required.
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree; registration on the ITU Registrar's Office system (sis.itu.edu.tr) PLUS separate MIAM portfolio submission. Handbook: 'portfolio submission is an additional requirement for candidates specifically applying to İTÜ MİAM's programs. Each candidate must also ensure that the official exam registration on the İTÜ Registrar's Office website is completed'. Written exams: 'General Music Knowledge and Music Theory Exams'; plus a Field exam for Sonic Arts; plus interview.
acceptsNonMusic: LIKELY YES — the Sonic Arts portfolio spec explicitly allows non-traditional and non-notated work and non-sonic elements: 'You can include non-sonic elements if these are an important part of your creative practice (e.g. video, architectural drawings, text), but overall the portfolio must demonstrate a clear interest in sound/music.' No music degree is stated as a prerequisite. NOT explicitly stated that a non-music bachelor is accepted — treat as UNVERIFIED on the formal rule, but the portfolio wording is unusually open. NOTE: candidate must still pass a 'General Music Knowledge and Music Theory' written exam.
portfolioSpec: VERBATIM: 'Applicants should submit a representative portfolio of creative work. The portfolio can include any of the following: electroacoustic or acousmatic compositions; sound installations; sound design; live performance(s); any other sound-based works using physical, digital, or electronic media; examples of creative audio coding / programming. You can include non-sonic elements if these are an important part of your creative practice (e.g. video, architectural drawings, text), but overall the portfolio must demonstrate a clear interest in sound/music. Please provide audio or audiovisual documentation as appropriate. You may also share examples of writing related to sound or music that you have produced (journal articles, reviews, curatorial statements etc.), though this is not required.' Submission: single zip/rar on Google Drive/Dropbox/OneDrive + passport photo, links entered in the MIAM application form.
auditionSpec: YES — entrance examinations. VERBATIM (2025-26 calendar): 'General Music Knowledge and Music Theory Exams' (3 hrs), then 'Field exams' for Master Programs: SED, Sonic Arts, Composition, then interviews. 'For Turkish candidates, entrance exams and interviews will be conducted in person at İTÜ Maçka Campus... International candidates have the option to do an online interview via Zoom as well.'
tuitionNonEU: 33,300 TRY per year for international students (from-abroad quota) at graduate level, entry 2024-25 / 2025-26 — approx. EUR 700-900/yr. Paid in two equal instalments. Rate for 2027-28 UNVERIFIED (set annually).

scholarships: Türkiye Bursları — fully funded: 100% tuition, monthly stipend '6.500 TL at Master's level', accommodation (dormitory year 1, then housing allowance 6,000 TL Istanbul/Ankara), once-off flight ticket, general health insurance, one year free Turkish language course. portfolioSpec: VERBATIM (translated from Turkish): pre-evaluation dossier requires (A) a digital copy of ONE work produced by the candidate reflecting interest/aptitude in the intended area — 'kendi ürettiği ses kayıt, ses programlama, çalgı yapım, ses elektroniği, akustik gibi alanlara yönelik tek bir çalışmasının' (a single work of their own in fields such as sound recording, sound programming, instrument making, audio electronics, acoustics) plus (b) an explanatory text of the work's content; (B) personal works in the field with audio files, software or written documents plus an index; (C) a CV. auditionSpec: YES — two-stage entrance exam. Stage I (written/oral, 6 areas): Müziksel İşitme (musical ear training — identifying musical elements in a played recording, 27 pts), Mesleki İşitme (professional listening — technically analysing/classifying/describing played sounds, 27 pts), Mesleki Bilgi (professional knowledge, 9 pts), Problem Çözme (9 pts), Analitik Düşünme (19 pts), Akademik Araştırmaya Yatkınlık (9 pts — candidates must read a named MA thesis in advance and answer a written question, then discuss it orally). Stage II: oral defence of the submitted dossier work + academic aptitude + review of the written exam (Ana Çalışma Yeterliği 57, Yazılı Sınav 28, Genel Değerlendirme 15). Entrance score = 10% dossier + 30% Stage I + 60% Stage II (the guide's summary table shows 10/70/20 — inconsistent in the source). Pass mark 60/100; final ranking = 70% entrance exam + 30% bachelor GPA.
